title: SG-5 · Data-driven layered scene renderer and interactive object system
summary: Generic Phaser-facing engine builds scenes from content, with layers, validated assets, interactive objects, effects and transitions.
description: Context: game/src holds engine/scene.ts (pure view/action logic), systems/*, a zod content schema (content/schema.ts) and a manifest loader with fallback (assets/loaders/manifestLoader.ts). The Phaser side (frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts) only reads state and renders nothing. Desired behavior: a generic engine under src/engine, src/scenes, src/entities and src/systems builds the bedroom from content definitions with nothing hardcoded in the scene class, renders ordered layers, preloads and validates assets with graceful fallback, supports interactive objects, dust and ambient light effects and scene transitions. Why: future AI cycles must add objects, characters and scenes by editing content and manifest only.
acceptance_criteria: Given a scene definition, when it is built, then every object becomes an entity with no object id referenced in engine code
Given objects on all six layers, when built, then display depth follows Background < Furniture < Interactive < Characters < Effects < UI Overlay
Given a missing asset, when a scene is built, then a fallback texture is used and no exception is thrown
Given an interactive object, when hovered, clicked, focused by keyboard or hidden by a visibility condition, then the correct highlight, label, event or removal occurs
Given effects and a goto_scene event, when handled, then dust, ambient light and a fade transition run from content data

preserve: Existing manifest schema and loader exports
Existing typed event bus in frontend/src/phaser/events.ts

technical_constraints: Phaser 3.90 pinned in frontend; game/ package has no phaser dependency so engine code uses structural types
Tests must mock Phaser, no browser
definition_of_done: All requirements have Act and Verify units green
Existing game and frontend unit tests still pass
non_functional: No memory leaks: entities destroy their listeners
